hourly.summary: United fans are greeting the international break with their trademark mix of gallows humour and injury anxiety. A 2-1 'smashing' of Lausanne (second-worst in the Swiss top flight, apparently) has convinced precisely nobody, while the treatment room reads like a full squad list — Dorgu, Mazraoui, Mainoo, Rashford, Sesko, both backup keepers... even the defenders are pulling up in friendlies. Throw in Ronaldo being labelled 'genuinely deranged' and a cryptic JJ Gabriel update, and it's the usual pre-weekend panic: will eleven fit bodies take the pitch on Saturday?

daily.summary: The day began with quiet optimism during the international break (7/10) as fans noted returning players and rivals' misfortunes, but sentiment sharply declined by afternoon into deep cynicism (4/10) over managerial speculation and structural flaws, ending in exasperation (4/10) at agent interference and ongoing ownership crises. The dominant arc is a collapse from fragile hope into the familiar 'crisis club' resignation, with only academy prospects offering any light.

weekly.summary: The week began with fleeting schadenfreude over Manchester City's 115 charges but rapidly curdled into a sustained cycle of aggrieved grievance — fixated on INEOS ownership, institutional bias, and United's own injury crisis. A brief mid-week recovery fueled by the women's derby win and transfer optimism proved short-lived, as the period closed in grim resignation: toxic outrage at Zirkzee and the regime settling into gallows humor that masks a fanbase that has normalized mediocrity and a 13-year title drought.
